novelty_check.method: public catalogue search (Hugging Face datasets, Zenodo, arXiv) plus web search for an existing ML-ready formulation of this exact task
novelty_check.ours: First public Australian trade-mark prosecution benchmark: per-application ever-registered outcome from filing-instant features only (sub-type, Nice classes and goods/services scope, mark-type flags, applicant metadata, filing channel, as-of applicant history), censoring-aware eligibility cutoff, standing-event labels that respect retroactive expungement, and temporal splits over decades of filings - built from IP Australia's weekly IP RAPID open data (CC BY 4.0). No AU register-outcome dataset with splits and a scored contract exists in ML-ready form.
prior_art: USPTO Trademark Case Files Dataset (Graham, Hancock, Marco, Miller 2013); 'Automating Abercrombie: Machine-learning trademark distinctiveness' (JELS 2023); IP Australia TM Checker (2021-); EUIPO/BOIP search-engine evaluations (ICAIL 2023)
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
novelty_check.theirs: IP Australia publishes the raw IP RAPID/IPGOD tables (weekly, CC BY 4.0) and a production tool, TM Checker, that flags registrability problems for a proposed mark from its text - a service, not downloadable labelled data with splits. The USPTO Trademark Case Files Dataset (Graham et al. 2013) is the same task family for the US register, and 'Automating Abercrombie' (J. Empirical Legal Studies, 2023) predicts USPTO distinctiveness refusals with train/val/test splits on US applications. A Kaggle re-upload (mgray39/ipgod2020) redistributes raw IPGOD2020 CSVs with no labels, splits or scoring contract.

prediction_question: For a trade mark application arriving at IP Australia on its application date (the filing date for direct Australian applications; the date it seeks protection in Australia for Madrid designations), will it ever achieve registration on the Australian Trade Marks Register, rather than ending before registration (refused, ex parte/inter partes refused, rejected, withdrawn, lapsed, not filed, cancelled, voided, or linked into another application)?
prediction_time: The application_date instant as defined by the publisher: 'The date at which the application arrived for processing to the IP Australia system... the filing or lodgment date of a direct application' (or the date an international right seeks protection in Australia). Everything used as a feature is on the application as lodged: IP right sub-type, Nice classes and goods/services scope from the application, mark-type flags and the presence of a word phrase, applicant metadata (organisation vs individual, country, state, postcode, ABN match) from the founding applicant, agent presence, filing channel (direct vs Madrid designation, convention priority, divisional parent), and derived applicant history computed strictly as-of the application date. Nothing observed after lodgement ships as a feature: examination events, adverse reports, acceptance, opposition, publication, status, gained_registration_status_date, gained_enforceable_status_date and deemed_retired_date are all post-instant by construction.

split_strategy: Candidate partition (to be confirmed by the worker aggregate-count job before status ready): filing-application_date windows train 1995-2013 / eval 2014-2018 / holdout 2019-2023, with an eligibility cutoff excluding filings whose outcome window is not yet closed at the extract date (pending share per filing year is being measured to set the cutoff; recent filings 2024+ are expected to be censored-heavy). Positives cluster in calendar time (examination practice changes, filing booms), so the conservative independent-positive count is per filing year, reported beside the row count. Splits are computed from the source by the worker job; both classes must be present in every window.
target_definition: Label: whether the application ever achieves registration - a standing (is_standing=TRUE) registered event in the trade-mark events table, cross-checked against the application table's gained_registration_status_date and current status. Retroactively expunged registrations (is_standing=FALSE - revocation that legally 'unhappened' the grant, per the dictionary's 'What is is_standing?' section) do NOT count as registered. Post-registration lifecycle (ceased/removed/expired after grant, non-use removal) does not change a positive label. Negative: application terminated before any registration (refused/rejected/withdrawn/lapsed pre-registration/not_filed/cancelled/voided/linked). Censored: applications with no registration and no pre-grant terminal event at the extract date (recent filings, or rare very slow prosecutions) - excluded by eligibility cutoff, never silently dropped. Label source columns (events, status, registration dates) are excluded from shipped features.
